A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Alman and Yu. The main text, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching definitions and proofs relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical hardness results and transformer constructions, not original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes. Empirical observations mentioned are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including Appendices A–D. It adds no original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The single-attention-unit constructions, matrices, and input/output MLPs are retained. v1 Theorems 4.2–4.3 become v2 Theorems C.1–C.2; the revised OV calculation does not change the specified construction.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. Document-similarity and inner-product problems remain theoretical objects; condensed application examples do not change evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Mamba and the other attention alternatives are discussed as prior work, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains empirical evaluation protocols, data splits, training budgets, or testing procedures. The mathematical parameter regimes are retained.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical case analyses appear in either version. The reorganized appendices contain theoretical definitions and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The principal hardness and expressivity conclusions are unchanged, and neither version reports empirical result entries. The altered intermediate OV proof bound is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1's proof adds the omitted ||v_j||_1 contribution from the value matrix and changes the no-instance bound from n/n^3 to nd/n^3. This is a local derivation revision, although the simplified display places an indexed norm outside its summation. The theorem statements and other proof arguments are retained across relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same SETH-conditional separation between truly subquadratic approaches and simple transformers on document-similarity problems. Theorems 1.1–1.4 retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 1.2 explicitly qualifies the language-task implication with 'when the input size is large enough.' This modestly clarifies applicability of the unchanged asymptotic bounds; the remaining interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: The mathematical construction details remain available, including those moved into appendices. Neither version supplies implementation instructions, experimental hyperparameters, hardware information, or code/data release information.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 adds Hu et al. (2024b) on LoRA computational limits and Hu et al. (2024c) on latent diffusion transformers. Appendix B also makes attribution to Karthik and Manurangsi more explicit. The central positioning against prior transformer limitations remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: background definitions and reductions move into Appendix A, and most Section 4 constructions move into Appendix C. Application examples are condensed, acknowledgements are removed, and citation and author-note conventions change. This is substantial restructuring despite largely retained prose and science.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout throughout, changing typography, text width, running headers, the title/author/abstract arrangement, and equation and reference layout. Several long bibliography URLs overflow the margins. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 partially addresses the omitted value-vector contribution in Theorem 4.1 and clarifies the large-input scope of the claims. The reorganized main text preserves supporting proofs, and the added citations improve context. These are limited gains: theorem conclusions remain unchanged, the revised calculation retains a summation-index inconsistency, and bibliography formatting introduces some overflow.
